theater: 基輔城與第聶伯河右岸

battle.name: 乞瓦之戰
battle.theater: 基輔城與第聶伯河右岸
battle.brief: 1240年12月6日，拔都的蒙古軍渡第聶伯河合圍基輔，白宦者愛德海督率攻城器械猛攻木柵土牆。城破後蒙古軍以油膏灌城縱火，連燒三日。這種以石油為膏的燃燒劑用法與拜占庭的希臘火同屬一門，卻頭一次大規模用於陸上攻城。基輔就此陷落，羅斯政治重心移向弗拉基米爾。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 交戰的兩方是蒙古帝國西部諸部——次年才正式立國的金帳汗國——與以基輔為核心的基輔羅斯，即羅斯諸公國的聯盟。蒙古方面由大汗窩闊台授權次子拔都統兵，拔都自1236年指揮西征大軍，1237年冬攻入羅斯腹地，先取梁贊與科澤爾斯克，1239年取佩列亞斯拉夫與切爾尼戈夫，1240年再取基輔；軍隊由本部蒙古騎兵、回回兵，以及西夏、契丹等降附的射手與工匠組成，攻城序列裡常配備俘獲的羅斯匠人。羅斯一方在1238年後已名存實亡：弗拉基米爾-蘇茲達爾、諾沃哥羅德、切爾尼戈夫、波洛茨克等公國相繼臣服，基輔大公國是最後一個尚能獨力抵抗的政體，城防由木柵、土牆與教堂的石築部分拼成，守軍是公國武裝侍衛與城內民兵，最高指揮是基輔大公與都主教。同一場戰役也牽動兩個遙遠方向：掌握希臘火配方的拜占庭尼凱亞流亡朝廷，1240至1244年間與蒙古互派使節；拉丁帝國與羅馬教廷則把蒙古人視為可以結盟的對象。這是一場草原國家直搗東歐基督教世界心臟的戰爭，戰場背後同時在計算希臘火的技術帳與拉丁騎士的效忠帳。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were the western part of the Mongol Empire — the polity that only in the following year became the Golden Horde — and Kievan Rus', the league of Rus' principalities centred on Kiev. On the Mongol side the army was led by Batu, the second son of the Great Khan Ögedei, who was given command of the western campaign in 1236: Batu entered the heartland of Rus' in the winter of 1237, took Ryazan and Kozelsk, captured Pereiaslav and Chernigov in 1239, and struck at Kiev in 1240. His force combined cavalry of the Mongol core, Huihui troops, and archers and craftsmen from Tangut and other peoples who had entered Mongol service; the siege train habitually included Rus' artisans taken alive. The Rus' side had been a name rather than a power since 1238: Vladimir-Suzdal, Novgorod, Chernigov and Polotsk had submitted in turn, and the Grand Duchy of Kiev was the last polity in the Rus' lands able to resist on its own, its defences a patchwork of timber palisade, earthen rampart and the stonework of its churches, manned by the armed retainers of the principality and the town militia, with the grand prince and the metropolitan as the supreme authority. The same campaign reached out towards two distant directions as well: the Empire of Nicaea, the Byzantine government in exile that guarded the formula of Greek fire, exchanged envoys with the Mongols between 1240 and 1244, while the Latin Empire and the Roman court read the Mongols as a power they might ally with. What was fought at Kiev was a steppe power striking at the heart of the Christian world of eastern Europe, with the technical arithmetic of Greek fire and the political arithmetic of Latin chivalry being worked out at the same time.
people: 蒙古方面的核心人物是拔都汗，窩闊台的次子，1236年受命西征，1240年冬自波蘭與匈牙利方向的戰線調頭北上，督率攻取基輔；編年史所記的攻城主將是拔都帳下的白宦者愛德海（Edagai），他率騎兵合圍基輔並督責攻城器械的使用，蒙古人每破一城即帶走工匠、射手與技師的做法，在這次攻城中留下痕跡。同一條西征線上，拔都之兄都倫可汗於1240年在中亞病逝，弟弟別兒哥則早於1223年的迦勒迦河之戰陣亡，可見1240年的基輔之戰正夾在蒙古第一次西征與1241年再攻歐洲之間。羅斯方面，基輔大公弗謝沃洛德在城破前離城，主教彼得亦攜教會財產北走，把都主教座堂從基輔遷到弗拉基米爾，羅斯教會的權威中心自此離開第聶伯河。加利西亞的丹尼爾王是記載中最接近現場的羅斯君主，他於1240年前後向蒙古人臣服，同時把基輔的陷落寫成哀歌，後世稱為《羅斯土地滅亡記》，一般認為作者與丹尼爾本人或佩切爾斯克修道院的修士有關；《伊帕季耶夫編年史》的作者勞倫季，則留下了記錄基輔陷落的唯一完整日誌。
peopleEn: The central figure on the Mongol side was Batu Khan, the second son of Ögedei, who had commanded the western campaign since 1236 and who in the winter of 1240 turned north from the Polish and Hungarian fronts to take Kiev. The commander named in the chronicles as the besieger of the city is Edagai, the white eunuch in Batu's service, who led the cavalry that surrounded Kiev and supervised the use of the siege engines; the Mongol habit of carrying off craftsmen, archers and technicians from every city they took is visible in this operation. On the same line of march Batu's brother Do'ürkhan died of illness in Central Asia in 1240, and their brother Bele had been killed at the battle of the Kalka in 1223, facts that place the siege of Kiev precisely in the gap between the first western campaign and the renewed drive into Europe in 1241. On the Rus' side the grand prince of Kiev, Vsevolod, left the city before it fell, and the metropolitan Peter likewise carried the property of the church away to the north, moving the metropolitan's seat from Kiev to Vladimir, so that the centre of Rus' ecclesiastical authority left the Dnieper for good. Daniel of Galicia was the Rus' ruler closest to the event in the sources: he submitted to the Mongols around 1240 and at the same time turned the fall of Kiev into a lament known as the Tale of the Destruction of the Russian Land, generally attributed either to Daniel himself or to a monk of the Pechersk monastery. Laurentius, the compiler of the Ipatiev Chronicle, has left the only complete contemporary day-book of the fall of the city.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是希臘火，即七世紀拜占庭人所用的銅管噴射式燃燒劑，配方屬帝國最高機密，填充以石腦油為膏、混入石灰與鹽，遇水不熄。基輔之戰並沒有拜占庭的銅管與海船參戰，希臘火本身不在攻城序列裡；它在這場戰役中的位置是技術源頭與事後對照。俄羅斯編年史記蒙古軍在基輔以油膏灌城燃燒、連燒三日，這種以石油為膏的縱火手法與希臘火同一門類，可以說蒙古西征沿途已把這類燃燒劑技術帶到了第聶伯河畔——同一條技術線在1258年的巴格達之圍有更明確的記載，蒙古攻城序列裡出現了裝填石油的縱火器與投擲袋。與此同時，羅斯一方並非全然無火器：《往古編年史》記1043年羅斯人自己也用火船對付君士坦丁堡，說明拜占庭的燃燒技術早經羅斯中介傳入東歐。除此之外，本戰的裝備由蒙古的複合弓、札甲與鱗甲、投石機與可移動的木製塔架、渡第聶伯河的浮橋，以及守方的木柵、土牆與教堂石壁構成，攻城器械的數目沒有留下記載。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is Greek fire, the incendiary mixture projected from bronze siphons by the seventh-century Byzantine state, whose formula was the empire's highest secret, a paste based on naphtha mixed with quicklime and salt that could not be put out with water. No Byzantine siphon and no warship of the empire fought at the siege of Kiev, and Greek fire itself was not part of the assault train; its place in this battle is that of a technical ancestor and of a later comparison. The Russian chronicles record that the Mongols poured a greasy oil over Kiev and burned it for three days, and this method of making fire from petroleum belongs to the same family as Greek fire: it may fairly be said that the incendiary technique had already been carried to the banks of the Dnieper along the Mongol line of march. The same technical line is documented more explicitly at the siege of Baghdad in 1258, where the Mongol siege train included naphtha-filled fire devices and throwing bags. The Rus' were not entirely without fire weapons of their own either: the Primary Chronicle records Rus' fire-ships used against Constantinople in 1043, which shows that the Byzantine art of burning had reached eastern Europe through Rus' intermediaries long before. Beyond that, the equipment of this battle consists of the Mongol composite bow, lamellar and brigandine armour, stone-throwing engines and movable timber towers, the pontoon bridges by which the Dnieper was crossed, and on the defending side the timber palisade, the earthen rampart and the stone walls of the churches; the number of siege engines used has not been preserved.
tactics: 蒙古的攻城法在此前三年已經定型：主力騎兵沿既定軸線疾進，靠連續的急行軍與佯退把羅斯諸城分割成孤立的靶子，再用大包圍斷其外援。基輔一戰是這套法子的收尾：拔都的騎兵自切爾尼戈夫方向逼近，渡第聶伯河時以舟船與浮橋維持渡過，遠征軍在城外展開，對基輔形成合圍；羅斯軍隊出城反擊的嘗試沒有成功，攻城軍的包圍圈反而收緊。攻城階段蒙古人倚靠投石機與火攻，先打擊木柵與土牆的接合處，再以火攻與撞擊配合壓垮木構防禦；城破之後的縱火是全城性的，把油膏灌入街巷與屋舍，以風助火勢。守方的部署以城內分區拒守為主，上城、波多利亞與佩切爾斯克城各成一個防禦節點，教堂與修道院被用作據點；都主教彼得帶著印璽與教會財產隨公國貴族先撤，說明城內已無成建制的指揮核心。編年史對攻城器械的細節著墨不多，能確定的只是這是一次短促的強攻，而非曠日持久的圍城。
tacticsEn: The Mongol way of taking towns had already been fixed during the three previous years: the main body of cavalry advanced along a set axis with all the speed it could, using continuous forced marches and feigned withdrawals to cut the Rus' towns apart into isolated targets, then closed in with a wide ring to cut off relief. The siege of Kiev was the closing piece of that pattern. Batu's cavalry closed in from the direction of Chernigov, kept the crossing of the Dnieper alive with boats and pontoon bridges, deployed the field army outside the city and closed a ring around Kiev; the Rus' attempt to sortie failed, and the ring of the besiegers tightened instead. In the assault the Mongols relied on stone-throwing engines and fire, striking first at the joints between timber palisade and earthen rampart, then combining fire and battering to crush the wooden defences. The burning after the breach was city-wide: oil was poured into the streets and into the houses, and the wind was used to spread the flames. The defence was arranged as a partition of the town, with the upper town, the Podil and the Pechersk fort each forming a node of its own, and churches and monasteries used as strongpoints; the metropolitan Peter carried off the seals and the property of the church with the princely party ahead of the rest, which shows that by then the city had no organised command core left. The chronicles say little about the details of the siege engines; what can be settled is that this was a short, violent assault and not a protracted blockade.
data: 可查證的數字有幾組。時間上，基輔陷落在1240年12月6日，攻城自前一日或數日前開始，《伊帕季耶夫編年史》記城破之後火燒了三日；同月蒙古軍尚在波蘭與匈牙利方向作戰，1241年4月的穆希戰役與9月的萊格尼察戰役都在其後。空間上，基輔位於第聶伯河右岸，蒙古軍自切爾尼戈夫方向沿河而下，渡河點與攻城營地的具體位置無記載；自拔都的根據地薩萊到基輔的路程約一千五百公里以上，而基輔到布達佩斯約一千一百公里，1241年蒙古軍正是沿這條路再往西。兵力方面，拔都西征大軍的總數沒有可靠記載，一般認為在十萬上下，但留在基輔城下作戰的只是分遣的一支偏師，其人數無從考證；蒙古軍攻城時把俘獲的羅斯工匠編入工程隊，是各編年史都提到的做法。損耗方面，蒙古軍的攻城器械數量、城牆缺口的寬度、撤退方向皆無記載；羅斯方面的指揮官姓名在編年史中僅記大公與都主教二人，軍官名冊已不可考。任何更精確的兵力、死傷與器械數字都是後世估算，不可當作史實。
dataEn: A few sets of figures can be verified. On timing: Kiev fell on 6 December 1240, the siege having begun on the previous day or a few days before, and the Ipatiev Chronicle records that the city burned for three days after it was taken; in the same month the Mongol army was still operating in Poland and Hungary, while the battle of Mohi in April 1241 and the battle of Legnica in September 1241 both came later. On space: Kiev lay on the right bank of the Dnieper, the Mongol army came down along the river from the direction of Chernigov, and the crossing point and the lines of the siege camp are not recorded; the road from Batu's base at Sarai to Kiev ran to something over fifteen hundred kilometres, while Kiev stands about eleven hundred kilometres from Budapest, and it was along that road that the Mongols marched again in 1241. On strength: there is no reliable figure for the total size of Batu's western army, which is generally put at around a hundred thousand, but only a detached column fought under Kiev, and its numbers cannot be checked; the chronicles all note that the Mongols enrolled captured Rus' craftsmen in the engineering teams. On losses: the number of Mongol siege engines, the width of the breach in the wall and the direction of the withdrawal are all unrecorded; on the Rus' side the commanders are named in the chronicle only as the grand prince and the metropolitan, the roster of officers being lost. Any more precise figures for men, casualties or machines are later estimates and cannot be treated as fact.
cause: 基輔之戰的直接起因，是拔都的西征軍在完成波蘭與匈牙利方向的掃蕩之後，需要把羅斯平原上的殘餘勢力收編，並打通西行的道路。自1236年入羅斯以來，蒙古軍先取梁贊、弗拉基米爾與科澤爾斯克，1239年奪取佩列亞斯拉夫與切爾尼戈夫，到1240年只剩下基輔還保留著羅斯諸公國最後的實體。基輔之所以成為最後的目標，除了它是羅斯的政治與教會中心、在編年史的敘事裡仍被視為「羅斯之母」之外，更實際的原因是地理：它扼第聶伯河與波羅的海、黑海商路的交會處，控制它就等於握住了基輔羅斯對外交通的樞紐。遠因則是蒙古帝國要在西亞與歐洲之間建立通道，1240年後不久，蒙古使者便出現在君士坦丁堡與亞歷山德羅的教廷，並向拉丁世界提出共同對付異教徒的號召。基輔的陷落，與其說是一場攻城戰的結果，不如說是蒙古西征把羅斯、匈牙利、波蘭與地中海世界一次拉進同一張地圖的第一步。
causeEn: The immediate cause of the battle of Kiev was that Batu's western army, having finished its sweep through Poland and Hungary, needed to bring the last powers of the Rus' plain under control and to open the road westward. Since entering Rus' in 1236 the Mongols had taken Ryazan, Vladimir and Kozelsk, had seized Pereiaslav and Chernigov in 1239, and by 1240 only Kiev still kept the last physical embodiment of the Rus' principalities. Kiev became the final target not only because it was the political and ecclesiastical centre of Rus' and was still treated in the narrative of the chronicles as the mother of Rus', but for a more practical reason as well: it commands the junction of the Dnieper with the trade routes to the Baltic and the Black Sea, so that holding it meant holding the hinge of Rus' communications with the outside world. The deeper reason lies in the Mongol intention to build a corridor between western Asia and Europe; not long after 1240 Mongol envoys appeared in Constantinople and at the papal court of Alexandria, calling on the Latin West to join them against the unbelievers. The fall of Kiev, rather than the outcome of a siege, was the first step by which the Mongol westward campaign pulled Rus', Hungary, Poland and the Mediterranean world onto a single map.
impact: 基輔陷落之後，羅斯的政治中心自第聶伯河轉移到東北的弗拉基米爾與西北的諾沃哥羅德，主教座堂北遷，佩切爾斯克修道院成為新舊兩地的精神中介；1326年都主教座堂再遷莫斯科，基輔在此後整整兩個世紀裡都只是金帳汗國的一個徵收點。文化的損失同樣深：城內的聖索菲亞大教堂、佩切爾斯克洞窟修道院與基輔的藏書在火中毀滅，抄本與工藝匠人四散，羅斯的正教傳統在往後兩百年只能靠北方與西方拼補。武器技術層面的後果更值得留意：蒙古西征把以石油為膏的燃燒劑技術帶到歐洲東境，1258年巴格達之圍即有蒙古軍使用這類縱火器的明確記載，而把這條技術線的源頭推到盡頭，正是拜占庭的希臘火——這門祕密技術在蒙古人手中脫離海船，變成可以在陸上城牆下使用的攻城手段。希臘火從海上的奇觀變成城市的災難，是這場戰役最耐人尋味的註腳。
impactEn: After the fall of Kiev the political centre of Rus' moved away from the Dnieper to the north-east at Vladimir and the north-west at Novgorod, the metropolitan's seat travelled north, and the Pechersk monastery became the spiritual link between the old lands and the new; in 1326 the seat moved again to Moscow, and for two full centuries after that Kiev was nothing more than a tax post of the Golden Horde. The cultural loss was no shallower: the cathedral of St Sophia, the Pechersk cave monastery and the book collections of Kiev were destroyed in the fires, manuscripts and craftsmen scattered, and for the next two hundred years the Orthodox tradition of Rus' could only be patched together from the north and the west. A consequence at the level of arms technology deserves particular attention: the Mongol campaign carried the art of the petroleum incendiary into eastern Europe, and the siege of Baghdad in 1258 gives explicit evidence of the Mongols using such fire weapons, while the source of that technical line, traced back to its beginning, is Byzantine Greek fire. The secret art detached itself from the sea and became a means of taking walled towns on land; Greek fire changing from a spectacle at sea into a disaster in the city is the most telling footnote to this campaign.
result: 結果是蒙古軍完勝，基輔在一場短促的攻城中陷落，城市被縱火焚燒，木構防禦與大量街區化為焦土。蒙古軍沒有在基輔長久停留：焚燒之後即轉兵西向，掃過沃里尼亞與加利西亞，又於1241年重新集結，向匈牙利與波蘭推進，最終在穆希與萊格尼察兩役被歐洲聯軍擋住；翌年因大汗去世而全軍東撤，基輔與羅斯全境淪為金帳汗國的附庸。羅斯方面的抵抗並未就此終結：加利西亞的丹尼爾一面臣服、一面維持著自己的權力，切爾尼戈夫與諾沃哥羅德亦在各自的形式下保存了殘餘的獨立性；但基輔一城再無單獨的守禦能力，編年史裡那句「基輔已逝」成為此後數百年羅斯人反覆引用的哀句。從裝備史的角度看，這場戰役真正的遺產是技術與示範：蒙古人向歐洲展示了以騎兵配合攻城器械、以火攻配合強攻的城市攻取方式，希臘火所屬的燃燒劑門類也隨之西傳。
resultEn: The result was a complete Mongol victory: Kiev fell in a short assault, the town was put to the torch, and its timber defences and a great part of its quarters were reduced to charred ruin. The Mongols did not stay long at Kiev; after the burning they turned their columns westward, swept through Volhynia and Galicia, and in 1241 gathered their strength again to push into Hungary and Poland, only to be checked by the European coalition at Mohi and Legnica. When the Great Khan died the following year the whole army withdrew eastward, and Kiev and all of Rus' became dependencies of the Golden Horde. Rus' resistance did not end there: Daniel of Galicia submitted while at the same time keeping his own power alive, and Chernigov and Novgorod preserved a qualified independence in their own forms; but Kiev as a single city could never again defend itself, and the line in the chronicles — that Kiev is gone — became a lament quoted again and again for the centuries that followed. From the point of view of the history of arms, the true legacy of this battle is technique and demonstration: the Mongols showed Europe how to take a city with cavalry and siege engines, with fire joined to a direct assault, and the class of incendiary to which Greek fire belongs travelled west with them.
